# Marketplace Requirements Quality Checklist: Bartr Smart Bartering Marketplace

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, and coverage of marketplace requirements before task generation, emphasizing trading integrity and AI bundle matching.
**Created**: 2026-11-14
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Focus**: Whole feature; primary emphasis on trading integrity and AI matching; supporting privacy, accessibility, and recovery coverage.
**Depth**: Standard.
**Audience / Timing**: Peer reviewer, after design and before task generation.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are member, item-owner, and trade-participant roles and their permitted access to each information category explicitly defined? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-015, Spec §FR-030, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the required listing information, draft/publication boundaries, and owner review or correction of assisted information fully specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-004, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK003 Are specific-product interests, category interests, explicit exclusions, and the relevance required for every incoming recommendation item documented? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-010, Spec §Scope and Exchange Rules]
- [ ] CHK004 Are supported bundle shapes, distinct ownership, participant count, size limits, and the common-community boundary explicitly stated? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009, Spec §FR-019, Spec §Scope and Exchange Rules]
- [ ] CHK005 Are allowed item/trade transitions and the point at which consent creates an all-or-nothing commitment fully documented? [Completeness, Spec §FR-020, Spec §FR-021, Spec §FR-029, Spec §Scope and Exchange Rules]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is the value-gap definition unambiguous about comparison currency, denominator, both members' limits, boundary inclusion, and rounding for presentation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, Spec §Scope and Exchange Rules; Matching/UI §Value Comparison and Recommendation Order]
- [ ] CHK007 Is a specific-product match defined precisely enough to distinguish two, one, or no benefiting participants, including additional matches and equal-priority ties? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010, Spec §Scope and Exchange Rules, Spec §Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK008 Are mandatory constraints clearly separated from interests and value-gap preferences that a manually composed offer may exceed? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018, Spec §FR-019, Spec §Scope and Exchange Rules]
- [ ] CHK009 Are assisted estimates, owner-entered values, unknown values, their dates, and uncertainty described without implying verified market prices or condition? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK010 Are the exact offer/listing changes that invalidate earlier consent distinguished from a replacement offer and from changes that leave an existing agreement intact? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016, Spec §FR-020, Spec §Assumptions]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 Is the accepted order of both-member specific matches, one-member specific matches, category-only matches, and percentage-gap tie-breaking consistent across the specification and supporting design? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010, Spec §User Story 2 scenario 10, Spec §SC-002; Plan §Semantic preparation and matching]
- [ ] CHK012 Are recommendation inspection, dismissal, sender consent, and mutual agreement consistently distinguished so that advisory suggestions never imply a commitment? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, Spec §FR-014, Spec §FR-020, Spec §Scope and Exchange Rules]
- [ ] CHK013 Are cancellation, pending handoff, mutual completion, and closed-history requirements consistent across the lifecycle definitions and participant journeys? [Consistency, Spec §FR-024, Spec §FR-025, Spec §FR-029, Spec §User Story 4]
- [ ] CHK014 Are current community/exclusion requirements and the preservation of already agreed terms consistent across profile changes, open offers, and historical records? [Consistency, Spec §FR-019, Spec §FR-022, Spec §FR-023, Spec §Assumptions]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK015 Are discovery and wording-match success criteria tied to predefined labeled examples, explicit thresholds, and coverage of all supported bundle shapes? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002, Spec §SC-003, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK016 Does the recommendation performance criterion define the population, inventory volume, concurrent demand, percentile, time limit, and treatment of failures unambiguously? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005; Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK017 Are onboarding, recommendation usefulness, comprehension, and negotiation-time criteria explicit about participant counts, rating scales, successful completion, and excluded waiting time? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, Spec §SC-006, Spec §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK018 Are accessibility and access-control success criteria stated as objective outcomes for the affected journeys and audiences? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008, Spec §SC-009, Spec §FR-028, Spec §FR-030]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK019 Do the primary journey requirements describe a complete path from inventory/preferences through negotiation, mutual agreement, and reported handoff, with each story independently understandable? [Coverage, Spec §User Stories 1–4]
- [ ] CHK020 Are alternate manual-entry and manually composed-offer requirements defined when image assistance, interpretation, or valuation is unavailable or uncertain? [Coverage, Alternate Flow, Spec §FR-004, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-013, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK021 Are exception requirements distinct for missing inventory, missing interests, missing values, a genuine no-match result, and incomplete or failed assistance? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-013, Spec §User Story 2 scenarios 7–9; Matching/UI §Completeness and HTTP Outcomes]
- [ ] CHK022 Are recovery requirements explicit about preserved information, an interrupted action's unresolved outcome, and the participant's permitted next step without assuming success or failure? [Coverage, Recovery Flow, Spec §FR-026, Spec §FR-027, Spec §User Story 4 scenario 3]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK023 Are requirements for overlapping commitments and repeated participant requests explicit about rejected alternatives, all-or-nothing reservations, and accurate resulting outcomes? [Coverage, Spec §FR-019, Spec §FR-021, Spec §FR-026, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK024 Are previously invalidated offers explicitly kept closed after an item becomes available again or an incompatible preference/community change is reversed? [Coverage, Spec §FR-022, Spec §FR-029, Spec §User Story 4 scenario 9; Model §member_policy_events]
- [ ] CHK025 Are cancellation and completion requirements defined for an unresponsive participant or competing decisions after the first handoff report? [Coverage, Spec §FR-024, Spec §FR-025, Spec §FR-029, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK026 Are zero, negative, unknown, and partly known bundle values addressed without presenting incomplete totals or percentages as certain? [Coverage, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-010, Spec §FR-018, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK027 Are dismissal requirements clear about which item or requester-preference changes permit a combination to return and which availability-only changes do not? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012; Matching/UI §Freshness, Dismissal, and Submission]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK028 Are data-purpose and audience requirements complete for relevant-interest explanations, full private preferences, coordination notes, historical images, and operational records? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015, Spec §FR-030, Spec §Key Entities; Providers §1. Boundary and correlation]
- [ ] CHK029 Are keyboard, screen-reader, responsive-review, consequential-action confirmation, and actionable status/error requirements defined for all core journeys? [Coverage, Spec §FR-028, Spec §SC-008; Matching/UI §Accessibility and Validation Boundaries]
- [ ] CHK030 Are availability, overload, retention, and recovery targets specified with clear scope, including preservation of commitments during restoration or rollback? [Measurability, Spec §FR-026, Spec §FR-029; Plan §Technical Context, Plan §Compatibility, rollout and recovery; Research §R10]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK031 Are assistance and semantic-discovery dependencies documented with their required capabilities, unavailable-service behavior, and distinction between prepared examples and real quality evidence? [Dependency, Spec §FR-004, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-013, Spec §Assumptions; Providers §8. Verification modes]
- [ ] CHK032 Is the plan's adult-only live-pilot assumption explicitly reconciled with the stated audience, account requirements, personal-data collection, and participant acceptance criteria? [Assumption, Spec §FR-001, Spec §Assumptions, Spec §SC-001, Spec §SC-006; Plan §Technical Context—Scale/Scope]
- [ ] CHK033 Are launch defaults and future-scope exclusions documented as bounded assumptions, including bundle limits, comparison currency, value-gap defaults, local handoff, and absent payment/shipping/dispute services? [Assumption, Spec §Scope and Exchange Rules, Spec §Assumptions]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK034 Are additional limits or obligations introduced during planning traceable to a requirement or an explicit assumption, with a documented way to resolve conflicts before dependent work? [Ambiguity, Spec §Assumptions; Plan §Constitution Check, Plan §Design and Delivery Boundaries]
- [ ] CHK035 Is the distinction between measurable discovery-quality targets and guarantees of exhaustive discovery or market fairness explicit and consistent across the requirements? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-011, Spec §SC-002, Spec §SC-003, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- All 35 items are newly generated and unchecked. Requirements have not been scored or approved by this checklist-generation command.
- Scope uses the whole-feature default offered in Q1; no narrower focus was supplied before generation. No extra must-have items were supplied with the command; the accepted recommendation-priority clarification is included.
- Scenario coverage includes primary, alternate, exception, recovery, and non-functional requirements.
- Source keys: [Spec](../spec.md), [Plan](../plan.md), [Model](../data-model.md), [Matching/UI](../contracts/matching-and-ui.md), [Providers](../contracts/provider-contracts.md), and [Research](../research.md). Section references identify the written requirements to review.
- Every item carries a source reference. A question about a possible gap or ambiguity is a review prompt, not a finding that the requirement is absent or defective.
- Reviewers may record supporting section references and findings inline. Mark an item `[x]` only after deciding that its requirements-quality criterion is satisfied; this never means implementation is complete.
- Leave items unchecked while clarification, correction, or reviewer assessment is pending. An agent may assist with assessment only when explicitly asked by the reviewer.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`; its existing content and state are preserved.
- No `tasks.md` exists yet. Task-level traceability can be added after task generation; this checklist assesses the current specification and design.
- CHK identifiers are sequential within this checklist. Later runs targeting this file must append items after CHK035 without replacing existing content or reviewer states.
